messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Increased OOM spike in us-west1-gpu pool (12 containers). Pattern: CUDA alloc failures + paged-attn slab alloc errors. Links: runbook://ooms and grafana://redwood/kvcache
alex (oncall): taking this. says who is on rotation for runtime?
priya: i'm available. seeing 504s for hosted model /v1/generate:gpt-j-13b on 3 tenants starting ~02:08 UTC
alex (oncall): priority check — customer impact? severity?
dave: customer-ops: customer-A and customer-B show 20-35% error increase, delayed responses up to 6s. marking SEV2 for customer-A. incident lead: alex
jamie: logs look like slow creep fragmentation hitting allocator thresholds. excerpt:
```
[2026-03-17T02:15:12Z] runtime: alloc failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
kv_cache: free_chunks=120 total_chunks=780 fragmentation=0.84
paged_attn: failed_alloc slab=32MB requested=256MB
```
alex (oncall): ok. quick mitigations: 1) bump KV eviction aggressiveness in pool, 2) enable model-fallback to smaller quant variant for long-request paths, 3) roll restart containers with frag>80% only if needed. can we do 1+2 immediately?
eng-runtime: rollout created: "kv-evict-bump-2026-03-17" targeting us-west1-gpu. Applying eviction policy: `evict_threshold=0.6` -> was 0.75. Also set fallback: `model_variant: gpt-j-13b-quant-small` for >200 tokens.
priya: pushing policy now (api -> /ops/pools/us-west1-gpu/evict). watching metric `kv_frag_percent` and `oom_count`
jamie: quick note — this is likely fragmentation from paged-attn allocator not reclaiming small slots; eviction helps reduce pressure but we should avoid full restarts unless fragmentation doesn't fall. I can instrument memstats on the hot nodes.
alex (oncall): good. runbook step: if eviction bump < 50% reduction in oom_count after 5m, escalate to drain + restart. otherwise proceed with fallback only.
dave: customer-ops: communicating to customer-A (ops@customerA) — they reported degraded latency. told them we have mitigation underway, next update in 10m.
incident-bot: update: eviction policy applied at 02:22 UTC.
priya: initial metric update: kv_frag_percent on top-affected nodes dropped from ~84% -> ~58% within 4m. oom_count reduced ~62%. errors for customer-A dropping.
alex (oncall): nice. keep monitoring. jamie — please open a postmortem ticket and take lead on allocator fix. we need better scavenging and a longer-term tweak to page slab sizing.
jamie: will do. immediate follow-up: push a conservative hotfix to staging for `slab_scavenge_ms=100` and add per-slab free lists reporting. If staging looks good, can schedule canary tomorrow.
eng-runtime: created ticket RN-INC-598765: "paged-attn allocator fragmentation leading to OOM; follow-up: scavenger, slot-coalescing". Assigned to jamie, due 2026-03-24.
incident-bot: NOTE: current error rate down 60% vs peak. Metric links: grafana://redwood/d/kv_frag and grafana://redwood/d/oom_counts
customer-ops: customer-A confirmed fewer errors after 02:27 UTC. still monitoring for edge cases.
alex (oncall): mitigation successful for now. summary: eviction bump + model-fallback reduced impact; no node cordon required. action items: jamie/priya postmortem + runbook update, add automatic eviction trigger when frag>0.8, longer-term allocator fix. tagging @eng-runtime for prioritization.
priya: logging traces and attaching heap snapshots to ticket RN-INC-598765.
jamie: noted. will include reproducer and perf regression checks in PR.
alex (oncall): i'll close this incident thread once postmortem ticket is created and customer ops confirms stabilization. thanks all :thumbsup:
